reviewer.actual_effort: low: I read each of the nine narrow PNGs once with Read. I had no crop or zoom tool and did not open any other file.

readings.name: jerusalem

marks.letters: י ר ו ש ל ם. Defective: no YOD between LAMED and final MEM
marks.VAV: shuruq (dot at mid-height beside the VAV)
marks.LAMED: qamatz, with meteg just left of it
marks.hiriq: one dot just left of LAMED's meteg, sitting between LAMED and final MEM, under the start of the MEM

unresolved: Which letter carries the hiriq (LAMED or MEM) cannot be told visually. It is printed past the meteg, toward the MEM.

marks.TET: qamatz with meteg directly to its left: METEG YES

marks.MEM: segol with a vertical meteg next to it: METEG YES

readings.name: bateinu

marks.BET: qamatz only. No meteg next to it
marks.TAV: dagesh dot inside the TAV: YES. Tsere with meteg beside it: METEG YES

unresolved: BET dagesh: I see no clear dot inside the BET, but this was not a target position, so I am not asserting it is absent.

marks.BET: sheva. No dot inside the BET: DAGESH NO. No meteg
marks.CHET: segol with meteg beside it: METEG YES

readings.name: tovim

marks.initial small letter: A short stroke with a head, hanging from the top of the line. It does not reach the baseline as a full VAV would. Sheva (two vertical dots) under or just right of it

unresolved: Initial letter: its shape is closer to YOD, but at this resolution I cannot rule out a reduced-size VAV. This stays open for human question 278. I did not settle it.

readings.name: tushbechan

marks.BET: sheva (dagesh possibly present, not a target)

unresolved: I can clearly see one dot at mid-height between TAV and VAV, plus the shin dot on top. I cannot confidently separate two dots here, one inside the TAV (dagesh) and one on the VAV (shuruq). This print puts the shuruq dot on the right of the VAV in jerusalem, so that one dot could be either. I lean toward both being present, as the primary reading says, but I am not confident.

readings.name: lehar

marks.LAMED: sheva. No meteg next to it: LAMED METEG NO

unresolved: HE meteg: I could not see a clear vertical stroke next to HE's patah. I cannot confirm the primary reading's 'HE patah + meteg YES'. I am not asserting it is absent either, because the stroke may be lost in the print texture.

readings.name: lanu

marks.LAMED: qamatz with meteg directly to its left: METEG YES

unresolved: LAMED dagesh: I cannot clearly see a dot inside the LAMED. I cannot confirm the primary reading's 'LAMED dagesh YES', and I am not asserting it is absent.

limits: I read each narrow PNG once at the size it displayed. I had no tool to crop or zoom further, so I cannot judge positions finer than about one letter width.

Telling which letter hosts a mark, and telling a dagesh from a shuruq dot next to it, depends on where things sit on the left or right. I have flagged every case where that decided the answer (tushbechan, the jerusalem hiriq).

Where I agree with the primary reading: jerusalem (defective, LAMED qamatz + meteg + hiriq), batachnu TET meteg, melekh MEM meteg, bateinu TAV dagesh + TAV meteg with BET qamatz and no BET meteg, bchesed no BET dagesh with CHET segol + meteg, lanu LAMED qamatz + meteg, lehar HE patah with no LAMED meteg.
Not confirmed: tushbechan TAV dagesh and VAV shuruq as two separate dots, the lehar HE meteg, and the lanu LAMED dagesh. The initial letter in tovim is still open.

These readings come only from the images. I did not use the Masoretic Text or any other occurrence of these words. I checked only the named target words, and I make no claims about the whole unit, the schema, or the export.
